title: Yolŋu present the Yirrkala bark petitions
summary: Yolŋu bark petitions reached Australia’s House of Representatives in August 1963, asserting relationships to land threatened by proposed bauxite mining.

claims.text: Yolŋu bark petitions reached Australia’s House of Representatives in August 1963, asserting relationships to land threatened by proposed bauxite mining.
Two bark petitions were tabled on different August dates. The record uses month precision to encompass both, rather than inventing a single presentation day.
Typed text and painted clan designs conveyed the petitioners’ case together. Buku-Larrŋgay Mulka describes this use of visual art as an assertion of political sovereignty.

review.corroboration: The National Museum’s account was compared with the Indigenous community art centre’s history. They agree on the 1963 petitions; the museum supplies parliamentary timing.
